intervals.note: The KEK history page lists the PS reaching its design beam in 1976 and records that 12 GeV was achieved the same year.
intervals.quote: The proton synchrotron (PS) produced an 8 GeV beam as designed.

intervals.label: experiments ended
intervals.note: The page states that experiments at the PS ended in December 2005; no source read states a formal decommissioning date.

name: KEK 12 GeV Proton Synchrotron
notes: No site is linked: the Atlas has no record of this machine's location on the KEK Tsukuba campus.

beam_energy.quote: KEK's facilities include a proton synchrotron accelerator which can produce an intense beam of 12 GeV protons.

summary.plain: KEK's first big accelerator, a proton ring finished in 1976. From 1999 it produced the neutrino beam for K2K, the first experiment to send neutrinos hundreds of kilometres to a distant detector. Experiments ended in 2005.
summary.technical: 12 GeV slow/fast-cycling proton synchrotron at Tsukuba, fed by a Cockcroft-Walton, a 20 MeV linac and a 500 MeV booster. Drove the K2K neutrino beamline from 1999 until the end of K2K data taking in November 2004; experiments ended in December 2005.
